Made in collaboration with ZeroOne Company, with Aleš as art director.

title: Cybertrends

more: A dark, calm base with a particle globe in the hero, soft teal and peach gradients, and quiet black and white photography. Each solution page follows the same rhythm: use cases, commercial value, partnership models and the products, so a partner finds their answer fast.

title: Cybertrends Brand Identity
lead: Brand identity for Cybertrends, a company building digital protection products. Security is a noisy, fear-driven category, so the identity is built around one idea: clear sight. It turns scattered risk into calm, real protection, without theatre or jargon.
more: The visual language comes from a single metaphor. Noise is the threat landscape, scattered grain with no shape and no meaning. The orb is the protection, grain gathering into a shell around what matters. Sight is the promise: what matters stays sharp and the rest falls back into grain.

That grain runs through everything, from particle type and the orb to photography treated with the same texture. The voice follows the same rule. Calm, clear and quietly confident: plain words, no dramatised threats, judged by what we remove, not what we add.

title: Asset Layout Editor
lead: Customers extend Ataccama ONE’s metadata model with custom properties, but the only way to surface them was a hidden JSON editor nobody outside engineering could use. I replaced it with a pin model: admins pick the properties that matter, and they appear at the top of every entity page of that type.
more: Grounded in research across 22 sources and six competitors, the layout stays locked with one clear escape hatch. No JSON, no code, delivered as a working prototype in six weeks.

title: Esens Letná
lead: Esens Letná is a new residential development in Prague’s Letná district. The brief was to translate that premium location into a web experience as confident as the apartments themselves. The design leans on three things: confident typography, full-bleed location photography, and generous whitespace that lets each section breathe.
more: The site is built around three pillars — Lokalita (location), Služby (services), and Byty (apartments). Each is treated as its own editorial chapter: location reads like a magazine spread, services like a curated menu, contact like a quiet conversation. Same brand voice, different rhythms.

I redesigned its website to present CFG as one confident, modern financial group, while giving each sub-brand, Comfort Money, Dluhopisomat, Srovnávač and more, a clear place in the story.
more: A system of deep forest green, warm cream and a single violet accent reserved for actions, set in Manrope and carried from the homepage through to the careers page.

title: Dluhopisomat
lead: Dluhopisomat opens corporate bonds to retail investors, a category long reserved for institutions. The product worked, but the brand wasn’t keeping up. I led a strategy-led redesign of the identity and the homepage, built around how trust is communicated to first-time investors.
more: After twelve directions across three palette families, the brand landed on deep teal with a confident green accent, everyday Czech photography, and a homepage that answers the trust questions before asking for anything.

title: Importing metadata in 3 clicks instead of 10
lead: Importing metadata is the first real thing a customer does in Ataccama ONE, and it took 6 clicks, sometimes 10, drilling into one connection at a time with no sense of where you were. I redesigned it as a single view of the whole source, connection, schema and table tree, with an import entry point right in the Data Catalog.
more: Designed in Figma, validated with consultants, then rebuilt as a working code prototype. Testing removed a preview step, and the measured flow went from 6–10 clicks down to 3.
meta: Product designer at Ataccama, owned the design end to end

title: Prague Pride Festival
lead: Over five years I contributed to the visual identity and graphics for Prague Pride Festival. The work evolved from agency collaboration to in-house development, encompassing complete campaign aesthetics across every media format.
more: Outputs spanned online campaigns, print, branded installations, stage designs, merchandise and spatial applications. The visual communication had to be both distinctive and flexible enough to adapt across surfaces. My thesis project went further: a comprehensive website redesign that examined nonprofit web patterns and optimised the festival’s communication and presentation.
Each year was an opportunity to advance the visual narrative around diversity, visibility and belonging through design.

title: Rezidence
lead: I designed a website for the sale of residential apartments, working closely with the art director. The core challenge was getting both the visual style and information architecture exactly right, meeting the developer’s brand requirements while staying attractive and clear for end clients.
more: The result reads as confident and editorial: clean typography, generous imagery, and a structure that lets prospective buyers find what they need without effort.

title: Geomap
lead: Complete website design for a geodetic office that builds on existing branding while establishing a distinct online presence. The challenge: addressing two audiences, end customers and corporate partners, with the same site.
more: Clarity, credibility, and professional brand representation were the through-lines across both B2C and B2B contexts.

title: Elspace
lead: Elspace asked for a redesign to simplify content and clarify their services. The original site lacked clear navigation, and prospective clients were leaving without understanding what was on offer.
more: The new design streamlined the offering, explained the collaboration process up front, and made it easy to evaluate whether Elspace was the right fit.

title: 1. Web IT
lead: A complete website redesign and brand refresh for 1. Web IT s.r.o., a development-first IT company. I drew from the company’s developer DNA, using IT-world visual metaphors: browser dialog boxes repurposed as CTA sections, code-styled accents, terminal-inspired typography.
more: The updated identity gave the brand a contemporary direction and a clearer voice. Collaboration continues to support the brand’s evolution while keeping it authentic.

title: Odstrčil, Craft Jewellery
lead: Complete UX/UI design for a craft jewellery maker’s website. The design emphasises visual cleanliness and elegance, a reflection of the precision and uniqueness of the work itself. Minimalism and air around each piece let the jewellery photography do the talking.
more: I conceived it primarily as a gallery experience rather than a traditional e-shop. The purchasing workflow stays intuitive without compromising the brand’s exclusivity or aesthetic.

title: Duhová stužka
lead: Visual identity and applications across formats, from web and print to social, for a Prague Pride campaign. The aim was a unified, clean visual with a clear message.
more: Restraint was the discipline: keep the system simple enough to scale, distinctive enough to recognise on any surface.

title: Prague Pride Merch
lead: Creative direction and design for the official Prague Pride Festival merchandise. I led the complete creative agenda, art direction, design, production, budget coordination, end to end.
more: The ‘Equality’ line combines distinctive visual design with authentic storytelling: celebrating diversity and supporting the community through merchandise that means something.
